observation: R172: the corrupted last-row prediction at the cache-c032 prefill varied between runs (60 in R165/R167b/R168/R170/R171/R173, 220 in R172) while everything else is deterministic; the new request inherits the finished request's attention blocks unzeroed (only the mamba block is zeroed); a full device barrier (R173) did not help; async scheduling off (R169) did.
hypothesis: Host-side race: with async scheduling the CPU rewrites reused pinned metadata buffers (block table, slot mapping, positions, token ids) for step N+1 while step N's non-blocking H2D copies of the same buffers are still queued, so the discarded step N runs with step N+1's metadata and writes into the new request's slots. Blocking copies remove the race.
decision: 64/64 with blocking copies -> race confirmed; then find the unguarded buffer and narrow the fix. Still failing -> deterministic-content path (block reuse without zeroing), test prefix caching / zero attention blocks.
